subject: BlueBridge cost synthesis + prioritized levers — next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@bluebridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T13:12:00Z
Subject: BlueBridge cost synthesis + prioritized levers — next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Short recap and recommended next steps so we have a single source of truth. I framed the economics around the two usage profiles you shared (customer support triage ~1.2M messages/mo and payment reconciliation batch jobs ~120k/mo) and the three levers we covered: model selection, batching/caching, and reserved capacity.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Immediate budget pressure for Q3: procurement target ~$30k/mo for inference.
- Latency sensitivity for support triage (95th percentile < 800ms).
- Need auditability and strict data controls for reconciliation flows.

Synthesis of economics (high level):
- Baseline hosted usage (no batching, gpt-style 16k context equivalent): ~1.6–1.9M tokens/day for triage -> estimated $42k–$55k/mo.
- With conservative batching (single-request batching window + auto-batcher) and prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, we can cut effective token spend by ~25–40% depending on cache hit rates; that brings triage into the $25k–$35k/mo range in most modeled scenarios.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) flips the unit economics for the reconciliation batch jobs — we estimate 40–60% cost delta versus hosted per-token, once committed capacity and expected throughput match your nightly window.

Priority levers I recommend we validate in a pilot (in order):
1) Prefix/KV caching for triage common templates (fast wins if you have repeated prompt structures).
2) Short-window batching for low-latency paths (trade a few ms for large token savings across spikes).
3) Evaluate a 3-month reserved pool for reconciliation with burst-to-hosted for irregular peaks.

Proposed next steps (asks from BlueBridge):
- Provide a small sample of triage prompts + metrics (token length distribution, traffic pattern CSV) so we can estimate cache hit potential.
- Confirm procurement timeline and any contracting constraints (PO vs. subscription).
- Security doc request list — you mentioned SOC2 attestation + specific logging needs; Marissa will follow up with the checklist.

Deliverables from Redwood by EOD Friday:
- A short workbook (attached) with three TCO scenarios (baseline, conservative savings, optimistic savings) and the assumptions called out.
- A one-page pilot plan (MVP scope, success metrics, duration) attached as "pilot-mop.docx".

Owner/contacts:
- Redwood technical lead (Rishi) — pilot sizing, model/ops assumptions.
- Redwood AE (Marissa) — contracting and procurement liaison.
- Ops point (Ben) — Dedicated sizing and burst policy options.

If that aligns, I’ll send a concise SOW template and a proposed pilot kickoff calendar.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@bluebridge.com>

Thanks Rishi — this is great and mirrors what we talked about internally. Quick clarifications:
- Procurement target is firm for Q3 at $30k/mo; we can stretch to $40k/mo with a business case.
- For triage, we have roughly 60% of tickets that follow 5 canonical templates — should be good cache candidates.
- Reconciliation is nightly but variable (peak month can be 2.5x normal).

I’ll send a stripped sample of 1,000 anonymized triage messages (redacted PII) and the monthly traffic CSV by Thursday. Can you confirm whether the prefix/KV caching changes any of our compliance obligations around token storage? We need to be explicit for InfoSec.

Also — would like a back-of-envelope on ROI: if we achieve a 30% token reduction on triage, what’s the expected breakeven period for pilot costs (rough PO + Redwood engineering time)? If you can add a simple breakeven row in the workbook that helps.

Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Product Ops, BlueBridge Finance
elena.soto@bluebridge.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@bluebridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: BlueBridge cost synthesis + prioritized levers — next steps

Elena — appreciate the quick reply and the specifics. Short answers:
- Prefix/KV caching does not change data residency controls; cached keys/values can be configured not to persist beyond the pilot and can be stored encrypted at rest under your KMS. We’ll document the default TTLs and options for rolling keys so InfoSec can review. Marissa will attach the compliance snippet.
- I updated the workbook with a breakeven row (see redwood_token_econ_snapshot.xlsx) — with conservative assumptions (30% token reduction on triage, $12k pilot engineering effort amortized over 12 months) the pilot pays back inside 3 months under the $30k/mo procurement target. Optimistic case is 6–8 weeks.

Operational asks to unblock procurement/PO:
- We need a signed NDA (you said legal would prefer a short form) — Marissa will send tonight.
- Pilot acceptance criteria: reduce triage token spend by >=20% OR keep latency 95th <= 800ms with savings visible in the first month.

Proposed kickoff calendar:
- Thu (7/8): share sample + traffic CSV (BlueBridge)
- Mon (7/12): review pilot sizing + finalize SOW (Redwood + BlueBridge)
- Mon (7/19): pilot kick (2–4 week run)

If that aligns I’ll book the sizing call (30m) for Monday 7/12 10:00am PT.

—Rishi
